newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU members told to clean up act on single market.
newsitem.headline: EU members told to clean up act on single market.

text.p: European Union countries were told on Friday to clean up their act and plug holes in the EU's border-free market ahead of the move to a single currency.

"The single currency is the optimisation and perfection of the single market which will enable it to develop its full potential," Mario Monti, the European Commissioner responsible for the market, told a news conference after a meeting of trade ministers.
He said it would be "deeply inconsistent" if, as the 15-nation Union forges on to new ambitions, its existing structures continued to have holes.
The single currency is due to come into effect on January 1, 1999, as the final stage of the European Union's Economic and Monetary Union.

Irish trade and tourism minister Enda Kenny said EU countries were unsatisfactorily applying the laws intended to create a border-free zone for goods, services, capital and people in both qualitative and quantitative terms.
"Most member states need to do better in quantitative and qualitative implementation," he told the news conference.

Monti said the EU countries' record had hardly improved since EU internal trade ministers met in May. So far only 93.3 percent of the legislation had been enshrined in national laws, he said, against 92.6 percent in May.

He unveiled plans for an information campaign to be launched on November 26, intended to show how the market -- which came into force on January 1, 1993 -- can help people in their daily lives, even if it is still far from perfect.

The campaign, with the help of a World Wide Web site, guides and telephone hotlines, will give information on living, working and studying in the EU, buying goods in other EU countries and making use of EU laws on health, safety and equal opportunities, Kenny said.

The EU ministers met counterparts from eastern Europe, who are queueing up for membership, and agreed to tighten adminstrative cooperation to allow the candidates to speed up preparations for taking on board the EU market legislation in time for entry.
